columns.name: Label shown on the plot.
columns.slowest_hz: Slowest known member of the class, Hz.
columns.example_hz: Value of the marked example object, Hz.
columns.max_hz: Maximum allowable spin (breakup), Hz; empty if none.
columns.source_url: Primary source for the values (journal DOI, agency fact sheet, spec sheet).
columns.citation: Short citation: authors, year, title, venue.
columns.notes: One line shown in the hover tooltip.

rows.name: H2 molecule
rows.citation: NIST Chemistry WebBook, H2 constants of diatomic molecules (Huber & Herzberg 1979)
rows.notes: Slowest nonzero spin is J=1: f = 2*sqrt(2)*B with B = 60.853 cm^-1; max is an order-of-magnitude estimate near the highest bound level

rows.name: Bacterial flagellar motor
rows.citation: Magariyama Y. et al. (1994) Very fast flagellar rotation. Nature 371, 752
rows.notes: Vibrio alginolyticus sodium-driven motor; tethered cells turn about 10 Hz

rows.name: Levitated nanoparticle
rows.citation: Ahn J. et al. (2020) Ultrasensitive torque detection with an optically levitated nanorotor. Nature Nanotechnology 15, 89
rows.notes: Laser-spun silica nanoparticle above 5 GHz; rim near the strength limit of silica

rows.name: Dental drill
rows.citation: Dyson J.E. & Darvell B.W. (1995) Dental air turbine handpiece performance testing. Australian Dental Journal 40, 330
rows.notes: Air turbines idle near 400000 rpm

rows.name: Ultracentrifuge rotor
rows.citation: Beckman Coulter, Optima MAX-XP benchtop ultracentrifuge specification
rows.notes: 150000 rpm and over 1000000 g

rows.name: Car wheel
rows.citation: UNECE Regulation No. 30, pneumatic tyres: speed category symbols (Y = 300 km/h)
rows.notes: 300 km/h on a 0.65 m tyre is about 40 turns per second

rows.name: Figure skater
rows.citation: Guinness World Records (2015) Fastest spin on ice skates: 342 rpm, Olivia Oliver
rows.notes: Record upright spin 342 rpm

rows.name: Wind turbine (15 MW)
rows.citation: Gaertner E. et al. (2020) Definition of the IEA 15-Megawatt Offshore Reference Wind Turbine. NREL/TP-5000-75698
rows.notes: 240 m rotor; 5.0 rpm at cut-in to 7.56 rpm rated

rows.name: Small asteroids
rows.citation: Warner B.D., Harris A.W. & Pravec P. (2009) The asteroid lightcurve database. Icarus 202, 134
rows.notes: Monolithic fast rotators; 2014 RC turns in about 16 s

rows.name: Rubble-pile asteroids
rows.citation: Pravec P. & Harris A.W. (2000) Fast and slow rotation of asteroids. Icarus 148, 12
rows.notes: Spin barrier near 2.2 h per turn

rows.name: Neutron stars
rows.citation: Hessels J.W.T. et al. (2006) A radio pulsar spinning at 716 Hz. Science 311, 1901; slowest: De Luca A. et al. (2006) Science 313, 814
rows.notes: PSR J1748-2446ad; slowest is 1E 161348-5055 at 6.67 h

rows.name: Stellar black holes (10 Msun)
rows.citation: McClintock J.E., Narayan R. & Steiner J.F. (2014) Black hole spin via continuum fitting. Space Science Reviews 183, 295
rows.notes: Horizon frequency for spin a from 0.12 to 0.998; size is the Schwarzschild diameter

rows.name: White dwarfs
rows.citation: Mereghetti S. et al. (2009) An ultramassive, fast-spinning white dwarf in a peculiar binary system. Science 325, 1222
rows.notes: HD 49798 companion turns every 13.2 s; cap is breakup for a 1.3 Msun white dwarf

rows.name: Rocky planets
rows.citation: Williams D.R., NASA Planetary Fact Sheet, NSSDCA (2024)
rows.notes: Venus (243 d) to Earth (sidereal day 23.93 h)

rows.name: Gas giants
rows.citation: Williams D.R., NASA Planetary Fact Sheet, NSSDCA (2024)
rows.notes: Uranus (17.24 h) to Jupiter (9.93 h)

rows.name: Sun-like stars
rows.citation: McQuillan A., Mazeh T. & Aigrain S. (2014) Rotation periods of 34,030 Kepler main-sequence stars. ApJS 211, 24
rows.notes: Kepler periods 0.2 to 70 d; Sun marked at 25.4 d sidereal

rows.name: Sgr A*
rows.citation: GRAVITY Collaboration (2022) Mass distribution in the Galactic Centre based on interferometric astrometry of multiple stellar orbits. A&A 657, L12
rows.notes: Mass 4.297e6 Msun; spin not measured so only the a = 1 cap is shown

rows.name: Betelgeuse
rows.citation: Kervella P. et al. (2018) The close circumstellar environment of Betelgeuse V. A&A 609, A67; radius from Joyce M. et al. (2020) ApJ 902, 63
rows.notes: About 36 years per turn; radius 764 Rsun

rows.name: M87* black hole
rows.citation: Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration (2019) First M87 Event Horizon Telescope Results. I. ApJL 875, L1
rows.notes: Mass 6.5e9 Msun; spin a from 0.5 to 0.94

rows.name: Magnetars
rows.citation: Olausen S.A. & Kaspi V.M. (2014) The McGill magnetar catalog. ApJS 212, 6
rows.notes: Periods 1.4-12 s; SGR 1806-20 marked at 7.55 s
